cues.subtitle: Alice, a commercial bank, and Hub, a dealer bank, register as entities on the Depository contract. Each entity is controlled by its own signing board.
cues.title: Two banks join the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Opening an account in the settlement system before a bank can settle there.
cues.what: Alice, a commercial bank, and Hub, a dealer bank, register as entities on the Depository contract. Each entity is controlled by its own signing board.
cues.why: Registration gives each bank an identity the Depository can verify. After it, payments between Alice and Hub happen in their bilateral account; only collateral and settlement go on-chain.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub each receive 1,000,000 USDC of test balance as reserves on the Depository.
cues.title: Test balances credited on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Alice and Hub each receive 1,000,000 USDC of test balance as reserves on the Depository.
cues.why: Only reserves moved into an account as collateral back bilateral exposure; the rest stays freely usable.

cues.subtitle: Alice opens one bilateral account with Hub. Both sides keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.title: Bilateral account opened
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral correspondent relationship, but with one co-signed record instead of two reconciled ledgers.
cues.what: Alice opens one bilateral account with Hub. Both sides keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.why: No network-wide registration and no shared ledger: the account involves exactly the two parties who carry its risk.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub each grant the other a 200,000 USDC credit line inside the account.
cues.title: Credit lines in both directions
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral credit limit, set by the bank that carries the risk.
cues.what: Alice and Hub each grant the other a 200,000 USDC credit line inside the account.
cues.why: Each bank sets the limit on what the other may owe it, and can lower it at any time; nothing is deposited.

cues.subtitle: Alice proposes a settlement: move 200,000 USDC of her reserve into the account as collateral. The amount is put on hold at once so it cannot be spent twice.
cues.title: Settlement proposed: reserve into collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Collateral locked per counterparty, earmarked while the instruction is matched.
cues.what: Alice proposes a settlement: move 200,000 USDC of her reserve into the account as collateral. The amount is put on hold at once so it cannot be spent twice.
cues.why: Hub's position only improves, so Hub signs automatically. A settlement is a shared proposal both banks must sign before anything reaches the chain.

cues.subtitle: Alice submits the signed settlement to the Depository. One transaction debits her reserve by 200,000 USDC and credits the account's collateral by the same amount.
cues.title: Collateral posted on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: Delivery of collateral against a signed instruction: final on-chain once the block is final; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.what: Alice submits the signed settlement to the Depository. One transaction debits her reserve by 200,000 USDC and credits the account's collateral by the same amount.
cues.why: The account now holds collateral that covers what Alice may owe Hub. The chain checks the signatures and that the amounts net to zero.

cues.subtitle: The inverse settlement moves the 200,000 USDC of collateral back to Alice's reserve through the same signed path.
cues.title: Collateral returned to reserve
cues.tradfiParallel: Releasing pledged collateral once the exposure it covered is gone.
cues.what: The inverse settlement moves the 200,000 USDC of collateral back to Alice's reserve through the same signed path.
cues.why: Collateral is not trapped, but it leaves the account only with the counterparty's signature. The on-chain balances return exactly to where they started.

cues.subtitle: On a local test chain, Alice and Hub each hold 1,000,000 USDC of test balance on the Depository and share one bilateral account with a 200,000 USDC credit line each way. They have already moved 200,000 USDC of collateral into the account and back out, each time with both signatures.
cues.title: Starting point: two banks, one account
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral relationship with credit limits both ways and collateral posted and released by mutual instruction.
cues.what: On a local test chain, Alice and Hub each hold 1,000,000 USDC of test balance on the Depository and share one bilateral account with a 200,000 USDC credit line each way. They have already moved 200,000 USDC of collateral into the account and back out, each time with both signatures.
cues.why: Collateral moves on-chain only through a settlement both banks sign; payments between them stay in the account.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Hub 60,000 USDC inside their account. Both sign the new account state; nothing goes on-chain. Alice now owes Hub 60,000 USDC, within the credit line Hub gave her.
cues.title: Alice pays Hub 60,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral payment on a credit line, confirmed by both banks at once.
cues.what: Alice pays Hub 60,000 USDC inside their account. Both sign the new account state; nothing goes on-chain. Alice now owes Hub 60,000 USDC, within the credit line Hub gave her.
cues.why: A payment inside an account changes only its net position.

cues.subtitle: Hub pays Alice 20,000 USDC over the same account, in the other direction. The two payments offset inside it.
cues.title: Hub pays Alice 20,000 USDC
cues.what: Hub pays Alice 20,000 USDC over the same account, in the other direction. The two payments offset inside it.
cues.why: Flows in both directions accumulate as one net position; only that would ever need settling.

cues.subtitle: 80,000 USDC of payments in both directions leave one net position: Alice owes Hub 40,000 USDC. Nothing has moved on-chain, and the debt is unsecured: the collateral went back to Alice's reserve.
cues.title: Net position: Alice owes Hub 40,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral net position waiting for settlement.
cues.what: 80,000 USDC of payments in both directions leave one net position: Alice owes Hub 40,000 USDC. Nothing has moved on-chain, and the debt is unsecured: the collateral went back to Alice's reserve.
cues.why: Hub carries this exposure within the credit line it granted. Settling it needs one transfer of the net amount, not one per payment.

cues.subtitle: Alice proposes to settle 20,000 USDC of her 40,000 USDC debt now: that amount would move from her reserve to Hub's, and her debt in the account would fall by the same. Hub's claim in the account would shrink, so Hub does not sign automatically.
cues.title: Negotiation opens: Alice offers to settle part
cues.tradfiParallel: A settlement instruction waiting for the counterparty's confirmation.
cues.what: Alice proposes to settle 20,000 USDC of her 40,000 USDC debt now: that amount would move from her reserve to Hub's, and her debt in the account would fall by the same. Hub's claim in the account would shrink, so Hub does not sign automatically.
cues.why: A bank signs only what it has decided to accept. An unsigned proposal moves nothing.

cues.subtitle: Hub replaces the terms: settle the whole net position. Alice pays 40,000 USDC from her reserve to Hub's, and her 40,000 USDC debt in the account is cleared. This is version 2 of the proposal, and Alice's 40,000 USDC goes on hold.
cues.title: Hub counter-proposes: settle the whole net
cues.tradfiParallel: Matching a settlement instruction between two back offices before it is released.
cues.what: Hub replaces the terms: settle the whole net position. Alice pays 40,000 USDC from her reserve to Hub's, and her 40,000 USDC debt in the account is cleared. This is version 2 of the proposal, and Alice's 40,000 USDC goes on hold.
cues.why: Both banks edit one shared proposal. Only the bank that did not make the last change can approve it, so nobody approves its own terms.

cues.subtitle: Alice signs version 2. The proposal now carries both signatures and a pre-signed account state for after the settlement.
cues.title: Alice approves
cues.tradfiParallel: A matched instruction, released for settlement with both counterparties' authorisation.
cues.what: Alice signs version 2. The proposal now carries both signatures and a pre-signed account state for after the settlement.
cues.why: It can now be submitted. If anyone stalls afterwards, the pre-signed post-settlement state still lets each side recover its funds.

cues.subtitle: Alice submits the agreed settlement. One Depository transaction moves 40,000 USDC from Alice's reserve to Hub's and clears the account's net position.
cues.title: The net position settles on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: Bilateral net settlement: final on-chain once the block is final; legal finality depends on system designation. Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Alice submits the agreed settlement. One Depository transaction moves 40,000 USDC from Alice's reserve to Hub's and clears the account's net position.
cues.why: 80,000 USDC of payments in both directions need one on-chain transfer of 40,000 USDC. This is bilateral netting only: there is no netting across other accounts.

cues.subtitle: The block is final. Alice's reserve fell by 40,000 USDC to 960,000 USDC, Hub's rose to 1,040,000 USDC, and neither bank owes the other anything in the account.
cues.title: Settled: the account is back to zero
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: The block is final. Alice's reserve fell by 40,000 USDC to 960,000 USDC, Hub's rose to 1,040,000 USDC, and neither bank owes the other anything in the account.
cues.why: The credit lines are still open, so new payments can build a new net position until the next settlement.

cues.subtitle: Alice proposes that Hub transfer her 1,000 USDC of reserves for nothing in return. It stays unsigned on Hub's side.
cues.title: A proposal Hub will not accept
cues.what: Alice proposes that Hub transfer her 1,000 USDC of reserves for nothing in return. It stays unsigned on Hub's side.
cues.why: A proposal is an offer, not an obligation. It cannot reach the chain without the counterparty's signature.

cues.subtitle: Hub rejects. The proposal is cleared on both sides and any amount held for it is released.
cues.title: Hub rejects: holds released
cues.tradfiParallel: An unmatched instruction cancelled; earmarked funds released.
cues.what: Hub rejects. The proposal is cleared on both sides and any amount held for it is released.
cues.why: Rejection is as explicit and signed as approval, so both sides agree that nothing is pending.
